title: Introduce connection dampener and soft-eviction safety net
author: Ariadne Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed a production incident (SUP-2178) where a burst of new websocket connections + heavy KV cache churn caused node-level latency spikes and a cascade of aggressive hard-evictions that impacted a subset of tenants in eu-west-1. This PR introduces a lightweight connection dampener at the runtime pool layer and a soft-eviction safety net that: 1) attenuates short-lived connection surges by pacing accepts per node, 2) favors tenant-preserving soft-eviction before hard eviction, and 3) exposes a regional hibernation signal to allow coordinated, graceful failovers to other regions.

Summary of changes: Added a new connection pool dampener implementation (dampener.go) that tracks short-window connection accept rates and temporarily applies token-bucket backpressure to the accept path when per-node connection velocity exceeds configurable thresholds. Implemented soft_evictor.go which introduces a two-step eviction pipeline: mark->soft-evict->monitor->hard-evict. Soft-evicted tenants are placed in a low-throughput quarantine with KV-cache held for a configurable grace window to enable fast restore. Instrumentation and alerts: updated SLO degradation alert rules to detect sustained soft-evictions and surface tenant-level signals to the control plane. Helm values: added knobs for production tuning (max_accept_qps, soft_evict_grace_secs, regional_hibernate_ttl). Integration tests simulate connection spikes and assert no immediate hard-evictions and that soft-eviction metrics are emitted.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement connection dampener and unit tests
- [x] Implement soft-evict pipeline and integration test
- [x] Add metrics and SLO alerts
- [x] Add Helm config with sane defaults and docs
- [x] Run e2e in staging (passed)
- [x] Backport plan for v1.24 (added to backport queue)

Commits (high-level):
- feat(dampener): add connection dampener with token-bucket pacing
- feat(evictor): introduce soft-evict pipeline and quarantine state
- docs(eviction): add metrics doc and operational notes
- ci(test): add integration scenario for connection spike
- helm: expose tunables in values-production.yaml

Files changed (high-level snippets):
- serving/runtime/connection_pool/dampener.go: new file (main algorithm ~120 LOC). Key functions: AcceptWithDampening(), sampleWindow(), admissionBackoff(). Uses a lightweight in-memory token bucket keyed by node ID and short TTL caches to avoid global locking.
- serving/runtime/eviction/soft_evictor.go: new file (pipeline glue). SoftEvict(ctx, tenantID) marks tenant and starts quarantine timer; MonitorQuarantine periodically evaluates restored throughput before clearing the mark.
- observability/alerts/slo-degradation.rules.yaml: added rule 'SLOSoftEvictionRateHigh' with 3m window and severity=warning.
- deploy/k8s/redwood-helm/values-production.yaml: added soft-evict and dampener knobs with recommended defaults tuned from staging runs.
- tests/integration/eviction_behavior_test.go: added test 'TestConnectionBurstDoesNotTriggerImmediateHardEvict' which spawns connections and verifies soft-evict trace and KV retention.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Rafael Ortega (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two comments: 1) ensure we don't unintentionally rate-limit long-lived healthcheck connections; 2) please add a metric for 'soft_evict_candidates' to help operators triage." 
- Author (Ariadne): "Addressed both: healthchecks are whitelisted based on header probe=true and 'soft_evict_candidates' metric added. Also updated docs with expected metric cardinality." 
- Leah Mwangi (reviewer): "Can we add a safety valve that auto-disables dampener if control-plane configured maintenance is in progress? Otherwise we risk interference during upgrades." 
- Author: "Added helm flag controlplane.maintenance_disable_dampener and a runtime override via control plane feature flag. Documented in metrics.md." 
- Jin Park (approver): "Integration runs green, and the staging incident replay looks good. Approving for merge. Consider follow-up: gradual rollout by region and a replayable incident runbook." 

CI summary: Initial CI run showed a flake in TestMetricsEmission (flaky test unrelated to feature). Re-ran tests; full CI passed (unit + integration + linters). Load test in staging: simulated 3x baseline connection velocity for 5 minutes; observed soft-eviction spike but no hard-eviction. Metrics: soft_eviction_rate peaked at 16% of affected tenants and decayed to <1% after 10 minutes.

Operational impact & rollout plan: This change is backwards-compatible and controlled via helm flags. Default behavior is conservative (dampener engages only at high velocity and soft-evict grace window set to 120s). Rollout plan: 10% of nodes in staging -> 25% canary in us-east-1 -> 100% eu-west-1; monitor SLO alarms for 30 minutes after each step. Backport: cherry-pick to release/v1.24 for immediate hotfix in affected customer clusters.

Release notes (for changelog): "Added connection dampener to reduce cascade hard-evictions during connection spikes and a soft-eviction safety net that preserves KV cache for tenants to enable fast recovery. Configurable via helm: max_accept_qps, soft_evict_grace_secs, regional_hibernate_ttl."

Post-merge actions: create Linear tasks for 1) telemetry dashboard for soft-eviction (ENG-4821), 2) controlled regional rollout and runbook (ENG-4899). Backport PRs opened to release/v1.24 and v1.23 (PRs: #183001, #183002).
